facts.text: NHTSA opened preliminary evaluation PE23-010 into Daimler Truck North America's Detroit Assurance AEB on 26 May 2023 after 18 owner complaints of activation without an actual roadway obstacle.
facts.quote: NHTSA opened preliminary evaluation PE23-010 on 26 May 2023 after 18 owner complaints of activation "without an actual roadway obstacle".

facts.text: The ODI resume for PE23-010 states that Detroit Assurance AEB may inaccurately identify an object and command the vehicle to stop unexpectedly.
facts.quote: The ODI resume says the system "may inaccurately identify an object and command the vehicle to stop unexpectedly"

facts.text: The ODI resume for PE23-010 gives an estimated affected population of 250,000 Freightliner Cascadia and Western Star 5700 trucks from model years 2017 to 2022.
facts.quote: gives a population of "250,000 (Estimated)" Freightliner Cascadia and Western Star 5700 trucks from model years 2017 to 2022.

facts.text: NHTSA's Vehicle Research and Test Center reproduced hard braking by Detroit Assurance AEB in a steel trench plate scenario.
facts.quote: NHTSA's Vehicle Research and Test Center reproduced hard braking in a "steel trench plate" scenario.

entities.name: NHTSA Vehicle Research and Test Center

facts.text: Daimler disputed the real-world relevance of the steel trench plate scenario used to reproduce hard braking by Detroit Assurance AEB, saying the plate was not representative of real-world driving.
facts.quote: Daimler said the plate was "not representative of real-world driving."

facts.text: In some events reported in the Detroit Assurance AEB investigation, the truck came to a complete stop in the travel lane.
facts.quote: In some reported events the truck came to a complete stop in the travel lane

facts.text: No crashes were reported when NHTSA opened PE23-010 into Detroit Assurance AEB on 26 May 2023.
facts.quote: no crashes were reported at opening [17, 18].

facts.text: On 23 October 2025, NHTSA upgraded the Detroit Assurance AEB investigation to engineering analysis EA25-006, covering trucks with Detroit Assurance 2.0, 4.0 and 5.0.
facts.quote: On 23 October 2025 NHTSA upgraded the case to engineering analysis EA25-006, covering trucks with Detroit Assurance 2.0, 4.0 and 5.0.

facts.text: By the 23 October 2025 upgrade of the Detroit Assurance AEB investigation, NHTSA had reviewed 347 vehicle reports and 32 consumer complaints.
facts.quote: By then NHTSA had reviewed 347 vehicle reports and 32 consumer complaints

facts.text: By the 23 October 2025 upgrade of the Detroit Assurance AEB investigation, 24 crashes, 13 injuries and one fatality had been reported.
facts.quote: with 24 crashes, 13 injuries and one fatality reported

facts.text: In the Detroit Assurance AEB investigation, NHTSA noted that trucks fitted with WABCO OnGuard showed markedly lower claim rates under similar operating conditions.
facts.quote: noted that trucks fitted with the WABCO OnGuard system showed markedly lower claim rates under similar operating conditions [19].

facts.text: Steel plates, grates and metal debris are everyday objects on construction and quarry sites.
facts.quote: Steel plates, grates and metal debris are everyday objects on construction and quarry sites

facts.text: The false-positive braking mechanism demonstrated in the Detroit Assurance steel-plate scenario should be expected off-road because steel plates, grates and metal debris are everyday objects on construction and quarry sites.
facts.quote: Steel plates, grates and metal debris are everyday objects on construction and quarry sites, so this false-positive mechanism should be expected off-road.

facts.text: NHTSA and FMCSA published a notice of proposed rulemaking for heavy-vehicle AEB on 6 July 2023.
facts.quote: NHTSA and FMCSA published a notice of proposed rulemaking for heavy-vehicle AEB on 6 July 2023 [20].

facts.text: For its heavy-vehicle AEB research, NHTSA started from light-vehicle AEB procedures and had to alter them for heavy-vehicle stopping distances, the test target and towing equipment.
facts.quote: NHTSA started from light-vehicle AEB procedures and had to alter them for heavy-vehicle stopping distances and for the test target and towing equipment

facts.text: NHTSA's heavy-vehicle AEB research encountered physical-facility limits near 100 km/h.

facts.text: Early heavy-vehicle AEB systems in NHTSA's research did not automatically brake when approaching a stopped lead vehicle.
facts.quote: Early heavy systems did not automatically brake when approaching a stopped lead vehicle

facts.text: A false-positive steel-plate scenario in NHTSA's heavy-vehicle AEB research generated forward-collision warnings.

facts.text: The cited 2021 Freightliner Cascadia AEB test series shows that success at higher speeds did not imply success at lower speeds.

facts.text: Track testing remained central throughout NHTSA's multi-year heavy-vehicle AEB regulatory research.
